label: Fictional training cases; authored hints and preset AI drafts

cases.title: A complete example: one month of a two-month service

facts.text: Fictional contract: service is provided uniformly during August and September 2026, with equal value in each month.
The total price for the two service months is AUD 600. What expense belongs to August?

evidence.text: Two service months, with equal service value in each.
Total service price: AUD 600.
Use the payment date alone to select the expense period.

rationales.text: The explicitly uniform service gives each service month an equal share of the total price.
Recognize the full price in whichever month payment occurs.

hints.L1: Compare the target month with the service dates and the total price.
hints.L2: Use the service delivery period; equal monthly allocation is justified here by the explicit uniform-service assumption.
hints.L3: There are two equally served months. Complete the calculation: 600 divided by __ months.
hints.L4: August expense is AUD 300: 600 / 2. The service and total-price facts support the uniform-service rationale.

cases.title: Review December expense despite a December invoice

facts.text: Fictional contract: service is provided uniformly in October, November, and December 2026, with equal value each month.
The three-month service costs AUD 1,200 in total.
October and November expenses have each already been correctly accrued. The question asks only for the expense belonging to December service.
The supplier issues the invoice in December.

evidence.text: Three months of equal service value, including December.
The total price is AUD 1,200 for the whole service period.
The prior two months were already correctly accrued; December is the target.
The invoice was issued in December.

rationales.text: Allocate by the explicitly uniform service period. The invoice month does not move October and November service into December.
The full invoiced total belongs to the invoice month.
Accruing prior months means no service expense remains for December.

hints.L1: Compare the invoice date with the service months and the prior accruals.
hints.L2: Identify the service delivered in the target month; the invoice date alone does not determine expense allocation.
hints.L3: Build an October–November–December table. Equal monthly service means 1,200 / __; the first two months are already accrued.
hints.L4: December expense is AUD 400: 1,200 / 3. Select service, total, and prior-accruals with service-not-invoice; correct the preset 1,200 draft.

aiDraft.text: Preset training draft with a deliberate error: record all AUD 1,200 as December expense because the invoice arrived in December.

facts.text: Fictional contract: service is provided uniformly from April through September 2026, six months with equal value.
The six-month service costs AUD 600 in total. What expense belongs to June?

evidence.text: June is one of six equally served months.
Total service price: AUD 600.
Reject a draft because it was produced by AI.

rationales.text: The stated equal monthly service supports 600 / 6; the draft agrees with the facts and can be accepted.
Reject every AI draft, regardless of its evidence.

hints.L1: Check the target month, the service duration, and the total.
hints.L2: Review the draft against the facts; agreement with an evidenced answer is a legitimate outcome.
hints.L3: June is included. Divide 600 by the number of equally served months: __.
hints.L4: June expense is AUD 100: 600 / 6. Select service and total with uniform-service and accept the correct preset draft.

aiDraft.text: Preset correct training draft: June expense is AUD 100 because the AUD 600 service is delivered equally over six months.

cases.title: Independent check: a changed service period

facts.text: A fictional company pays AUD 900 in December 2026.
The payment covers service in January, February, and March 2027 only, delivered uniformly with equal monthly value. No service is delivered in December 2026.
What expense belongs to December 2026? Only judge expense allocation; no journal entry is requested.

evidence.text: The service starts in January; December has no delivered service.
The question is about December expense.
Payment happens in December.

rationales.text: No service has been delivered in December, so none of the price belongs to December expense.
The payment month receives the full expense.
Divide the price by three and assign a share to December even though service has not begun.

hints.L1: Compare the service start date with the target month's end.
hints.L2: Expense follows the stated service delivery, rather than the cash payment date.
hints.L3: List only the months in which the contract says service is delivered. Is December on that list?
hints.L4: December expense is AUD 0 because service begins in January. Select service and target with service-not-started. These hints are available only after leaving the independent challenge or submitting.

cases.title: Pause when milestone performance is unknown

facts.text: A fictional AUD 1,200 contract delivers work against milestones; it does not specify equal monthly service.
The supplied documents omit acceptance records and performance progress for December.
Can the expense belonging to December be determined from these documents?

evidence.text: Delivery depends on milestones, rather than equal monthly service.
Acceptance and progress information is missing.
The total price is AUD 1,200.

rationales.text: Request acceptance or performance-progress evidence before determining the target-period amount; uniform allocation is not supported.
Assume three equal months and divide the total by three.
Missing evidence proves that no service occurred.

hints.L1: Look for evidence that a milestone was delivered or accepted in the target period.
hints.L2: Do not assume uniform monthly performance for a milestone contract.
hints.L3: The total price is known, but which records establish the December performance? Identify what is missing.
hints.L4: Choose need_info with a null amount. Select milestones and missing-performance with need-performance, and request acceptance or performance-progress records.

aiDraft.text: Preset training draft with a deliberate error: allocate AUD 400 to December by assuming three equal months.

cases.title: Retention check: January's share of a three-month service

facts.text: Fictional contract: service is provided uniformly from 1 December 2026 to 28 February 2027, with equal value in each of the three service months.
The three-month service costs AUD 1,500 in total.
What expense belongs to January 2027? The dates are fictional case facts, not a request to change the demonstration clock.

evidence.text: January is one of three months of equal service value.
Total service price: AUD 1,500.
The question asks only for January expense.
Discard December because it is in a different calendar year.

rationales.text: Allocate the total over all three equally served months, including the month in the prior calendar year.
Divide by only January and February because they are in the target calendar year.

hints.L1: Count all the service months, including the one before the year boundary.
hints.L2: Use the stated service period and equal monthly value; the calendar-year boundary does not remove a service month.
hints.L3: The period contains December, January, and February. Complete 1,500 / __ for January.
hints.L4: January expense is AUD 500: 1,500 / 3. Select service, total, and target with uniform-service. An incorrect independent submission demonstrates support restoration.
